neighbours.label: the word that completes a restrictive, small-quantity phrase after 'only' or 'rarely' (only one of, only rarely, only a little, only about 2% ... is), as against the same sentences with a full or large quantity
fire: Dozens of letters were sent, but only one of them reached the king.
In the dry season the village sees rain only rarely.
The medicine helped only a little with the cough.
Of all the applicants, only two of the women were hired.
Only about 5% of the beach is open to the public.
We visit my uncle in the mountains only occasionally.
The new paint is only slightly darker than the old one.
Many seeds were planted, only a few of which sprouted.
quiet: Dozens of letters were sent, and all of them reached the king.
In the wet season the village sees rain every afternoon.
The medicine helped a great deal with the cough.
Of all the applicants, most of the women were hired.
About 95% of the beach is open to the public.
We visit my uncle in the mountains every summer.
The new paint is much darker than the old one.
Many seeds were planted, and nearly all of them sprouted.

predictions: fire 0.3-1.3 on of/rarely/little/is after 'only'; 'all of', 'a lot', 'every week' versions below 0.05
